newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU drops dumping duties probe into Korean diggers.
newsitem.headline: EU drops dumping duties probe into Korean diggers.

text.p: The European Union said on Thursday it had dropped anti-dumping inquiries into imports of hydraulic diggers weighing more than six tonnes from South Korea.

European Commission investigations, sparked by a complaint in December 1994 from the Committee of European Construction Equipment on behalf of EU digger manufacturers, concerned imports of self-propelled tracklaying and other hydraulic excavators with 360 degree revolving superstructures.
"The Commission, having concluded its investigation, informed the complainant of the results thereof. The complainant subsequently withdrew the complaint," the Official Journal said.

The 15-country EU regularly imposes anti-dumping duties against product imports from other countries, arguing that products have been "dumped" on EU markets at prices designed to undercut local manufacturers or which are subsidised by higher prices on exporters' protected home markets
Anti-dumping duties, permitted under World Trade Organisation rules, are a controversial trade defence mechanism increasingly used around the world.
